days.label: The first market day
days.about: Eke opens the izu. The dataset calls it the main Igbo market day and links it with the east and with fire.

line.igbo: Eke bụ isi ahịa ndị Igbo.
line.en: Eke is the main Igbo market day.

days.label: The second market day
days.about: Orie is the second day of the izu. Many towns hold markets, meetings and even festivals on it.

today.igbo: Taa bụ Orie, ahịa anyị ga-azụ n'uju.
today.en: Today is Orie, our market will operate fully.

line.igbo: Ndị obodo m ga-eme mmemme iri ji ọhụrụ ha n'ụbọchị ahịa Orie.
line.en: My community will celebrate their new yam festival on Orie market day.

days.label: The third market day
days.about: Afọ is the third day of the izu. The dataset links it with the north and with earth.

today.en: Today is Afọ. Will you come?

line.igbo: Anyị ga-ezukọ ọzọ n'ụbọchị Afọ, n'izu a.
line.en: We will meet again on Afọ day, this week.

days.label: The fourth market day
days.about: Nkwọ closes the izu. Some of the largest markets, Onitsha's among them, open on Nkwọ.

today.igbo: Taa bụ Nkwọ, ahịa Emekuuwku ga-azụ n'uju.
today.en: Today is Nkwo, the Emukwu market will operate in full.

line.en: The Onitsha market sells on Nkwor.

beliefNote: In older Igbo belief each market day is also tied to a spiritual force, which the dictionary calls an arụsị. We share this as history and belief, and it is never a game piece here.
